title: Associate, Early Careers — Engineering, Global Services & Support
description: Early Careers at SmartDocs: Show Us Who You Are Freshers and final-year students welcome · No experience required · Apply with a 2–3 minute phone video Who we are SmartDocs builds procurement, contract management and spend management software for public sector organizations: state agencies, toll road authorities, cities and utilities. Our customers use our platform to buy goods and services, manage contracts and pay suppliers responsibly with taxpayer money. We work on Java, Angular, SAP integrations and Azure, and we use AI tools every day in how we design, build and support our products. We're hiring a group of early-career people to grow into technical roles with us. We care far more about how you think, learn and communicate than about what's already on your resume. The three tracks We're hiring into three areas. You don't need to have everything figured out. Tell us what interests you, and we'll work out the best fit together. People can and do move between tracks as they grow. 1. Associate Developer You'll learn to build software the way it's increasingly being built: working alongside AI coding agents, reviewing and improving what they produce, and owning features end to end. Good fit if you like building things and want to write code for a living. 2. Global Services Analyst You'll help customers get SmartDocs up and running: understanding how their procurement and finance teams work, configuring the platform, testing, and doing some light development where needed. Good fit if you like technology and people roughly equally, and enjoy solving business problems. 3. Global Support Analyst You'll be the person customers turn to when something isn't working: investigating issues, finding root causes, fixing what you can and working with developers on the rest. Good fit if you like puzzles, are patient, and get satisfaction from making a problem go away. Who should apply Recent graduates or students in your final year of college A degree (or degree in progress) in engineering, computer science, IT, science, maths or a related field. If your degree is something else but you're genuinely technical, apply anyway and tell us why. Curious about how technology works, and willing to learn things nobody has taught you yet Clear communicator in English, spoken and written No work experience is needed. Really. How to apply: send us a 2–3 minute video Instead of a cover letter, we'd like to see and hear from you. Record a short video on your phone introducing yourself. No editing, no fancy setup, no special software. Just you, talking to us. This is not a technical test. We're not going to quiz you on code. We want to get a sense of who you are before we meet you. What to talk about Use these as a guide. You don't need to cover them in order, and you don't need to cover all of them. Who you are. Your name, where you're from, what you studied or are studying. Something you figured out on your own. A project, a problem you solved, something you taught yourself, something you built or fixed. It doesn't have to be technical or impressive. We want to hear how you approached it. Why SmartDocs, and why this kind of work. What draws you to it? Which track interests you most. Or tell us you're not sure yet and what you're weighing. Both are fine answers. One thing we wouldn't learn from your resume. A few tips Keep it between 2 and 3 minutes. Shorter is better than longer. Talk, don't read. Notes are fine, but please don't read from a script, whether you wrote it or an AI did. We want to hear you think. Find a quiet spot with decent light. Face a window rather than having it behind you. Hold your phone steady (propping it up works) and look at the camera. One take is fine. We'd rather see the real you than a polished performance. How to submit Upload your video to hr@smartdocs.ai Name the file: FirstName_LastName_Track.mp4 (for example, Priya_Sharma_Developer.mp4 , or _Undecided if you're not sure) Attach your resume (one page is plenty) Include your graduation year and a phone number we can reach you on What happens next We'll watch every video. If we'd like to take things forward, we'll invite you for a conversation with our team, followed by a short practical exercise based on the track you're interested in. We aim to get back to everyone within asap SmartDocs is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds. We're looking forward to meeting you.

description: Dear candidate, Please find the JD for the AI Developer role below, let me know if you have any questions. Role Summary We are looking for an AI Developer to design, build, and run agentic AI systems: software agents that plan, call tools, use company data, and complete multi-step tasks with controlled human oversight. You will work with several model providers and model sizes, choosing and routing between them for quality, speed, cost, and data-handling needs, ensuring no single model or vendor becomes a point of failure. This is a hands-on engineering role. You will write production code, build evaluation harnesses, and take agents from prototype to a monitored, secure, and supportable service. Key Responsibilities Agent design and build • Design and build agents and multi-agent workflows that plan, use tools, keep state, and complete multi-step business tasks. • Choose the right pattern for each problem (single agent, workflow with fixed steps, supervisor and worker agents, human-in-the-loop approval) and explain the trade-offs. • Write and maintain prompts, system instructions, tool definitions, and structured output schemas as versioned code. • Build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and memory components, including document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector or hybrid search, and citation of sources. Multi-model strategy and orchestration • Work with several model families and providers (for example Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini, and open-weight models such as Llama or Mistral) through hosted APIs, cloud platforms (AWS Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, Google Vertex AI), and self-hosted inference. • Build a model abstraction and routing layer that selects models by task type, quality, latency, cost, context length, and data-residency rules, with fallbacks when a provider fails or rate-limits. • Benchmark models on our own tasks and data, record the results, and re-evaluate when new models or versions are released. • Manage cost and latency through caching, batching, prompt compression, smaller models for simple steps, and token budgets. Tools and integrations • Connect agents to enterprise systems through REST and SOAP APIs, databases, message queues, files, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or equivalent tool standards. • Design tools with clear contracts, least-privilege access, input validation, idempotency, and safe handling of errors and retries. • Build integrations for document processing, search, email and messaging, workflow engines, and line-of-business applications such as claims, policy, and finance systems. Evaluation and quality • Build evaluation suites with golden datasets, automated checks, model-graded and human review, and regression tests that run on every change to prompts, tools, or models. • Measure task success, accuracy, groundedness, tool-call correctness, latency, and cost, and report them to stakeholders. • Run red-team and adversarial tests, including prompt injection, data leakage, and tool misuse. Safety, security, and governance • Apply guardrails: input and output filtering, permission checks before actions, approval steps for high-impact actions, and audit logs of every agent decision and tool call. • Protect personal and health data (PII and PHI) through masking, access control, encryption, retention rules, and region-appropriate hosting, in line with applicable regulations (for example data-privacy law and sector rules such as IRDAI). • Document model choices, known limitations, and risks, and support internal AI governance and model risk reviews. Operations and collaboration • Deploy agents through CI/CD pipelines to cloud or container platforms, with tracing, monitoring, alerting, usage and cost dashboards, and incident runbooks. • Provide L2/L3 support for agent incidents and carry out root-cause analysis, including bad outputs, tool failures, and model regressions. • Work with business owners, product managers, security, data, and integration teams to scope use cases, define success metrics, and plan rollout. • Review code and designs, mentor developers new to LLM engineering, and keep technical documentation and an internal catalog of agents, tools, and approved models. Required Qualifications • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience). • 4+ years of software development experience, including 1+ year building LLM-based applications that reached production. • Strong Python (and/or TypeScript or Java) with clean, tested, maintainable code. • Hands-on experience building agents with tool or function calling, structured outputs, and multi-step workflows, using a framework (for example LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, CrewAI, or a vendor agent SDK) or custom orchestration. • Practical experience with at least two model providers or families, and an understanding of their differences in context length, tool-use behavior, cost, latency, and data-handling terms. • Experience with RAG: embeddings, vector or hybrid search, chunking strategies, and retrieval quality tuning. • Experience designing evaluations for LLM systems (test sets, automated and human review, regression checks). • Strong API and integration skills (REST, JSON, OAuth2, webhooks) and SQL. • Working knowledge of Git, CI/CD, containers (Docker), and at least one cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud). • Understanding of LLM security risks (prompt injection, data leakage, excessive agent permissions) and of handling sensitive data. Preferred Qualifications • Experience running open-weight models (for example with vLLM, Ollama, or managed endpoints) and knowledge of quantization, serving, and GPU cost trade-offs. • Experience with fine-tuning or adapting models (LoRA, preference tuning, distillation) and judging when it is worth doing instead of prompting or RAG. • Experience with model gateways and routing tools (for example LiteLLM, or cloud-native gateways) and with observability tools for LLM tracing (for example Langfuse, LangSmith, or OpenTelemetry-based tracing). • Experience with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), agent-to-agent protocols, and building shared tool servers. • Experience with document AI: OCR, extraction from forms and PDFs, speech-to-text, and multilingual content. • Background in insurance, healthcare, or financial services, including claims, policy, or customer-service workflows. • Knowledge of AI governance frameworks and regulation (for example the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001, or local data-protection and sector rules). • Experience with event-driven systems (Kafka, RabbitMQ, or cloud queues), workflow engines, and Kubernetes. • Relevant certifications (cloud, AI or ML, or security). title: AI Engineer
description: Job ID 74192 Category Global Data Insight & Analytics Location Chennai, India Work Type On-site Your primary mission will be to design, build, and take to production Generative AI tools and Large Language Model (LLM) applications that assist our analytical modelers in their day-to-day work — AI co-pilots for code generation, automated model-documentation and validation generators, and monitoring agents. You will own these solutions end to end: from architecture and model selection through cloud deployment, evaluation, observability, cost efficiency, and secure operation at scale on Google Cloud Platform. Beyond individual delivery, you will raise the bar for the team — defining engineering standards, reviewing designs, mentoring engineers, and partnering with platform, security, and model risk stakeholders so that GenAI capability lands in production safely and stays reliable. GenAI Solution Architecture: Architect and build production-grade LLM-powered applications, multi-agent systems, and workflow automations that assist model validators and quantitative modelers (e.g., independent validation agents, code-generation agents, monitoring agents). Own the technical design end to end, including model selection, prompting and orchestration strategy, retrieval design, tool integration, and evaluation criteria. Agentic & Retrieval Systems: Design agent architectures with clear tool boundaries, guardrails, and fallback behaviour. Build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines over internal data, including chunking strategy, embedding selection, index design, hybrid search, and grounding/citation quality. Define how agents are evaluated for correctness, hallucination, and safety before release. Cloud Platform & Deployment Architecture: Design and operate highly available, multi-service AI workloads on Google Cloud Platform. Take ownership of the cloud architecture for AI applications — compute and serving patterns (Cloud Run, GKE), networking (VPC, private service access, egress controls), identity (IAM service accounts, least privilege), secrets (Secret Manager), storage and data services (GCS, BigQuery), and managed AI services (Vertex AI, Vertex Vector Search). Make deliberate trade-offs on scalability, latency, resilience, and cost. AI-Ops & LLMOps at Scale: Establish and mature AI-Ops/LLMOps pipelines covering the full lifecycle of Generative AI tools: automated deployment, model and prompt versioning, artifact and evaluation tracking, regression testing of prompts and agents, and continuous monitoring for quality, drift, latency, token cost, and hallucination mitigation. Build the reusable platform components that let other engineers ship GenAI safely without rebuilding foundations. CI/CD & Infrastructure as Code: Own CI/CD and infrastructure automation for AI services using Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Cloud Build, Kubernetes manifests) and GitOps practices. Deliver reproducible, auditable, environment-parity deployments with automated testing, progressive rollout, and clean rollback paths. Containerization & Performance Engineering: Package and serve AI applications as containerized microservices (Docker/Kubernetes), tuning autoscaling, resource requests and limits, cold-start behaviour, concurrency, caching, and batch versus real-time serving patterns. Drive down inference cost and latency without compromising quality. Observability, Reliability & SRE: Instrument AI systems with structured logging, distributed tracing, metrics, alerting, and dashboards. Define SLIs/SLOs for AI services, run incident response and root-cause analysis, and design for graceful degradation when upstream model providers or quotas fail. Security, Governance & Model Risk: Ensure every AI solution meets Ford's data privacy, security, compliance, and model-risk standards. Implement guardrails for internal data usage, prompt-injection and data-leakage protection, PII handling, access control, and audit trails — and produce the documentation and evidence needed for governance and audit review. Technical Leadership & Mentorship: Provide technical direction across the AI engineering team: set coding, architecture, and evaluation standards; conduct design and code reviews; mentor engineers and modelers on GenAI engineering practice; and translate ambiguous business problems into scoped, sequenced technical roadmaps. Act as a trusted reviewer for peers and a bridge between analytics, platform, and risk stakeholders. User-Centric Collaboration: Partner closely with analytical modelers to understand their daily bottlenecks, data prep challenges, and coding workflows, and convert those pain points into measurable AI products. Define success metrics up front and validate impact after adoption. Skills & Knowledge LLM & GenAI Technologies: Strong hands-on experience with LLM orchestration and agent frameworks (e.g., Google ADK, MCP), prompt and context engineering, function/tool calling, and working with both commercial and open-source foundation models — including reasoning about model capability, context limits, latency, and cost. Cloud Platform (GCP): Strong hands-on experience designing and operating on Google Cloud Platform: Cloud Run, Cloud Build, GKE, GCS, BigQuery, Vertex AI, Vertex Vector Search, IAM, VPC networking, Secret Manager, and Artifact Registry. Comfortable contributing to cloud architecture decisions — service selection, networking topology, quota management, and cost optimization. AI-Ops / LLMOps: Working knowledge of tools and platforms for model deployment, prompt and model versioning, evaluation harnesses, tracing, and monitoring of LLM and GenAI outputs in production. Experience defining evaluation datasets, automated scoring, and quality gates for GenAI releases. DevOps, IaC & SRE Practices: Good proficiency in CI/CD tooling, GitOps, containerization (Docker), orchestration (Kubernetes), Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), and cloud-native monitoring, logging, and alerting. Vector Databases & Retrieval: Experience with vector search and embedding technologies (e.g., Vertex Vector Search, sentence transformers) and the retrieval patterns that sit on top of them — hybrid search, re-ranking, and grounded generation. Software Engineering: Strong hands-on Python engineering (5+ years), building APIs (FastAPI, Flask) that serve AI models to end users, with good typing, testing, packaging, and code-review practice. Enough full-stack understanding to integrate front-end, back-end, and AI services reliably. Security & Compliance: Familiarity with cloud security practices, identity and access management, secrets management, network policies, and compliance requirements in regulated environments. Analytics Workflow Understanding: Familiarity with the workflows of data scientists and modelers (data wrangling, feature engineering, model validation) so you can build tools that fit how they work. Qualifications & Experience Education: Master's or Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Cloud Computing, or a related technical discipline. Overall Experience: 6–9 years of software engineering, AI/ML, or cloud engineering experience, with experience owning systems in production. GenAI Production Experience: Around 3 or more years of hands-on experience building and deploying LLMs and Generative AI applications in production, including experience taking a solution from concept into production and iterating on it with users. Cloud & Platform Engineering: Experience building and operating AI/ML workloads on a major cloud provider (GCP preferred), including CI/CD for AI, containerization (Docker/Kubernetes), infrastructure as code (Terraform, Cloud Build, GKE), and production observability. Seniority & Scope: Experience leading technical work: contributing to architecture, helping set engineering standards, reviewing designs, mentoring engineers, and working effectively across teams. Comfortable working with independence and navigating some ambiguity. Communication: Ability to explain technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders — modelers, risk and governance partners, and leadership — and to work with them to agree priorities. Good to Have: Exposure to the Banking, Financial Services, or Credit Analytics industries; familiarity with SAS to help build code-translation or modernization tools for modelers; experience with machine learning engineering and model serving frameworks; and any relevant cloud certification (e.g., Google Cloud Professional Cloud Architect, Professional Machine Learning Engineer, or Professional DevOps Engineer).

title: Data Scientist
description: You are a hands-on Data Scientist with 5+ years of experience applying statistics, machine learning, and analytics to solve business problems. You are skilled at translating ambiguous questions into analytical approaches, exploring complex data, and communicating actionable findings. You understand data engineering concepts and can work with data pipelines and cloud platforms to prepare reliable datasets and support model deployment. You enjoy collaborating across disciplines and taking ownership from problem definition through measurement of business impact. Responsibilities Partner with business stakeholders to frame problems, define success metrics, and translate business needs into analytical and data science solutions. Perform exploratory data analysis, statistical analysis, hypothesis testing, and experimentation to identify patterns, drivers, and opportunities. Design, develop, evaluate, and refine machine learning and statistical models for use cases such as forecasting, classification, segmentation, and anomaly detection. title: Data Scientist
description: Job Requirements To drive the end-to-end development, scientific evaluation, and product lifecycle management of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) systems as part of an R&D organization. The Mid-Senior Data Scientist plays a key role in translating clinical, scientific, customer, and product requirements into robust AI/ML solutions and generating the scientific evidence required to demonstrate their performance, safety, reliability, and suitability for the intended use. The role requires a combination of strong Data Science and machine learning expertise, practical experience in clinical science, biomedical research, medical technology, or a related applied research environment, and the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary product development teams. The candidate is expected to take ownership of assigned AI/ML components and scientific workstreams, from defining algorithm concepts and development strategies through data curation, algorithm development, performance characterization, verification and validation, and lifecycle monitoring. They should be capable of independently driving technical and scientific activities while collaborating closely with Data Scientists, clinical and domain experts, product management, software engineering, and quality and regulatory functions. A PhD is welcome but is not a prerequisite. Demonstrated experience in applied clinical or biomedical research, scientific evidence generation, and cross-functional product development is particularly valuable. What are my responsibilities? Lead the translation of customer needs, intended use, clinical or technical requirements, and applicable regulatory considerations into measurable algorithm performance targets and product requirements. Drive the definition of AI/ML development and scientific evaluation strategies for assigned algorithm components, ensuring alignment with the overall product and clinical development strategy. Work closely with research scientists, medical experts, product managers, and other stakeholders to understand clinical workflows, relevant endpoints, use cases, and the scientific context in which algorithms will be used. Independently conduct exploratory data analysis and comprehensive data risk assessments to identify data gaps, quality issues, potential bias, confounding factors, outliers, and limitations that may affect algorithm development and evaluation. Define data requirements, sourcing strategies, cohort composition, subgroup representation, and acceptance criteria for training, tuning, and independent evaluation datasets, ensuring alignment with the intended use and target population. Lead the specification and quality assurance of annotations, including annotation guidelines, acceptance criteria, inter- and intra-annotator variability, and quality control processes. Collaborate with internal and external clinical experts, data providers, and annotation suppliers. Establish and maintain representative, well-documented, and version-controlled data cohorts, ensuring data provenance, traceability, integrity, and fitness for purpose throughout the development lifecycle. Design, implement, train, optimize, and technically characterize AI/ML algorithm components using appropriate machine learning, deep learning, statistical, and generative AI methods. Identify and assess suitable emerging AI technologies, including foundation models, Large Language Models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), model adaptation, fine-tuning, and Agentic AI approaches, where relevant to the product use case. Define scientifically justified performance metrics, evaluation methodologies, test cases, and acceptance criteria to assess algorithm performance, including accuracy, robustness, reliability, generalizability, explainability, bias, and subgroup performance. Plan, lead, and execute reproducible scientific evaluations and bench tests using representative datasets and relevant subgroups as part of the overall verification and validation strategy. Interpret scientific and technical evaluation results, conduct detailed error and failure-mode analyses, investigate unexpected findings, and derive evidence-based recommendations for algorithm improvements and product decisions. Assess the clinical and practical relevance of algorithm performance, including the implications of model limitations, data characteristics, and potential failure modes in the intended use environment. Contribute to the design and execution of clinical investigations, reader studies, retrospective or prospective studies, and other evidence-generation activities required to establish algorithm performance and clinical relevance. Collaborate with clinical research and domain experts to ensure that scientific evaluation approaches, study protocols, endpoints, and interpretations are methodologically sound and relevant to real-world use. Take ownership of Data Science work products and scientific documentation, including data management information, data and annotation specifications, algorithm development documentation, scientific evaluation protocols, test cases, and scientific evaluation reports. Provide scientific and technical input into product reviews, design reviews, verification and validation activities, and regulatory submissions. Support responses to questions concerning data, annotations, methodology, clinical relevance, and algorithm performance. Work closely with software engineering and MLOps teams to establish reproducible development pipelines, versioned datasets and models, experiment tracking, automated testing, controlled deployment, and integration of AI/ML components into products. Contribute to the definition and implementation of lifecycle monitoring strategies, including metrics and mechanisms for detecting data anomalies, changes in data distributions, performance degradation, and algorithm drift. Identify technical, scientific, clinical, and data-related risks early and proactively communicate their potential impact on algorithm development, product performance, and regulatory objectives. Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior Data Scientists, support knowledge sharing, and contribute to the development of scientific and technical best practices within the R&D organization. Stay up to date with advances in Data Science, AI/ML, clinical research, biomedical science, and applicable regulatory expectations, assessing their relevance and potential application to ongoing and future product development. Qualification Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Biomedical Engineering, Medical Informatics, Biomedical Sciences, Clinical Research, or another relevant quantitative, scientific, or engineering discipline. A PhD is welcome but not required. Equivalent professional experience in clinical science, biomedical research, medical technology, applied AI/ML research, or a related scientific and technical environment is highly valued. The candidate should have a strong foundation in: Probability, statistics, experimental design, and scientific methodology. Artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning. Linear algebra, optimization, and numerical methods. Data structures, algorithms, and software programming. Clinical research methodology, biomedical research, or applied scientific investigation. Model evaluation, interpretation of empirical results, and evidence-based decision-making. Experience Level This is a Mid-Senior R&D position. The candidate is expected to have approximately 4–8 years of relevant professional experience in Data Science, AI/ML, clinical science, biomedical research, medical technology, or a related applied research and product development environment. The emphasis is on demonstrated ownership and practical experience rather than academic qualifications or years of experience alone. Particularly relevant experience includes: Hands-on development and scientific evaluation of AI/ML models in applied research or product development environments. Experience working with clinical data, biomedical datasets, medical imaging, healthcare applications, or other domain-specific scientific data. Experience designing or contributing to clinical studies, scientific investigations, or structured evidence-generation activities. Experience translating clinical, scientific, or customer requirements into technical specifications and measurable performance criteria. Experience collaborating across multidisciplinary teams, including clinical experts, researchers, engineers, product management, and quality and regulatory stakeholders. Experience taking AI/ML solutions from research and prototyping towards product integration, verification, validation, and deployment. Candidates with a strong background in clinical research, biomedical engineering, medical informatics, or applied healthcare AI are particularly encouraged, even if their professional experience is not exclusively in traditional Data Science roles. Desired Knowledge & Experience Strong understanding of machine learning, deep learning, statistical analysis, experimental design, and scientific evaluation methodologies. Active programming skills in Python and practical experience with libraries and frameworks such as NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Keras. Demonstrated experience in the end-to-end AI/ML development workflow, including data preparation, model development, training, tuning, evaluation, error analysis, reproducibility, and technical documentation. Proven ability to independently define and execute scientific evaluation strategies, including performance metrics, evaluation cohorts, subgroup analyses, test methods, and acceptance criteria. Practical experience in clinical science, biomedical research, medical technology, healthcare AI, or another domain-specific applied research environment. Understanding of clinical research principles, including study design, clinical endpoints, patient populations, data interpretation, and the assessment of clinical relevance. Experience working with clinical or biomedical data, including an understanding of data quality, representativeness, bias, confounding factors, annotation quality, data provenance, and traceability. Demonstrated ability to translate scientific and clinical questions into technical problems and to communicate algorithm performance, limitations, and implications to multidisciplinary stakeholders. Experience contributing to scientific publications, clinical investigations, research reports, technical documentation, or other structured evidence-generation activities. Knowledge of medical device software development, AI/ML product lifecycle management, and relevant quality and regulatory frameworks is an advantage. Familiarity with MLOps concepts and tooling, including source and data versioning, reproducible pipelines, experiment tracking, automated testing, CI/CD, deployment, and performance monitoring. Hands-on experience with current Large Language Models and Generative AI, including foundation models, prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, model adaptation, and fine-tuning. Knowledge of Agentic AI, including tool-using models, multi-step workflows, orchestration, memory, and autonomous or semi-autonomous decision paths, is an advantage. Experience with systematic evaluation of LLM, Generative AI, and Agentic AI systems, including task-specific benchmarks, groundedness, factuality, robustness, reproducibility, human evaluation, safety and guardrail testing, tool-use correctness, and failure-mode analysis. Experience with databases and query languages such as SQL; knowledge of Kusto Query Language, Snowflake, or graph databases such as Neo4j is an advantage. Exposure to cloud-based data and AI environments, preferably Microsoft Azure, including Azure Blob Storage, Azure Databricks, Azure Data Factory, Azure Machine Learning, Azure Monitor, or Azure DevOps. Experience working with structured and unstructured data, including clinical datasets, medical imaging, machine logs, event data, Parquet files, text data, or multimodal data. Knowledge of healthcare, medical technology, clinical data, or interoperability standards such as DICOM, HL7, or FHIR is preferred. Familiarity with medical device development standards and regulatory frameworks, such as ISO 13485, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, and applicable AI-related regulatory requirements, is an advantage. Experience coordinating scientific and technical workstreams, managing project deliverables, and aligning priorities across cross-functional R&D and product development teams. Required Soft Skills & Other Capabilities Strong scientific mindset, analytical thinking, critical reasoning, and attention to detail, with the ability to challenge assumptions and draw objective conclusions from empirical evidence. Ability to independently drive scientific and technical workstreams, take ownership of deliverables, and make well-founded decisions within an agreed scope. Strong interdisciplinary mindset, with the ability to bridge Data Science, clinical science, biomedical research, software engineering, product development, and regulatory considerations. Proven ability to collaborate effectively with clinical experts, researchers, Data Scientists, software developers, product managers, and quality and regulatory stakeholders. Ability to understand and appreciate clinical and scientific context, translating complex domain-specific problems into practical and technically sound AI/ML solutions. Commitment to scientific integrity, reproducibility, traceability, data quality, and responsible AI development. Curiosity and resilience to investigate unexpected results, identify root causes, challenge established approaches, and continuously improve algorithms based on scientific evidence. Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, including the ability to assess technical and scientific risks, identify dependencies, and propose practical solutions. Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including the ability to present and explain complex scientific methods, clinical context, technical results, uncertainties, limitations, and risks to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Ability to take initiative, manage competing priorities, and work independently while recognizing when alignment or guidance from senior technical, clinical, product, or regulatory stakeholders is required. Willingness to share knowledge, mentor junior colleagues, and contribute to a collaborative, scientifically rigorous, and innovation-driven R&D culture.

title: Data Scientist
description: Job Requirements To drive the end-to-end development, scientific evaluation, and product lifecycle management of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) systems as part of an R&D organization. The Mid-Senior Data Scientist plays a key role in translating clinical, scientific, customer, and product requirements into robust AI/ML solutions and generating the scientific evidence required to demonstrate their performance, safety, reliability, and suitability for the intended use. The role requires a combination of strong Data Science and machine learning expertise, practical experience in clinical science, biomedical research, medical technology, or a related applied research environment, and the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary product development teams. The candidate is expected to take ownership of assigned AI/ML components and scientific workstreams, from defining algorithm concepts and development strategies through data curation, algorithm development, performance characterization, verification and validation, and lifecycle monitoring. They should be capable of independently driving technical and scientific activities while collaborating closely with Data Scientists, clinical and domain experts, product management, software engineering, and quality and regulatory functions. A PhD is welcome but is not a prerequisite. Demonstrated experience in applied clinical or biomedical research, scientific evidence generation, and cross-functional product development is particularly valuable. What are my responsibilities? Lead the translation of customer needs, intended use, clinical or technical requirements, and applicable regulatory considerations into measurable algorithm performance targets and product requirements. Drive the definition of AI/ML development and scientific evaluation strategies for assigned algorithm components, ensuring alignment with the overall product and clinical development strategy. Work closely with research scientists, medical experts, product managers, and other stakeholders to understand clinical workflows, relevant endpoints, use cases, and the scientific context in which algorithms will be used. Independently conduct exploratory data analysis and comprehensive data risk assessments to identify data gaps, quality issues, potential bias, confounding factors, outliers, and limitations that may affect algorithm development and evaluation. Define data requirements, sourcing strategies, cohort composition, subgroup representation, and acceptance criteria for training, tuning, and independent evaluation datasets, ensuring alignment with the intended use and target population. Lead the specification and quality assurance of annotations, including annotation guidelines, acceptance criteria, inter- and intra-annotator variability, and quality control processes. Collaborate with internal and external clinical experts, data providers, and annotation suppliers. Establish and maintain representative, well-documented, and version-controlled data cohorts, ensuring data provenance, traceability, integrity, and fitness for purpose throughout the development lifecycle. Design, implement, train, optimize, and technically characterize AI/ML algorithm components using appropriate machine learning, deep learning, statistical, and generative AI methods. Identify and assess suitable emerging AI technologies, including foundation models, Large Language Models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), model adaptation, fine-tuning, and Agentic AI approaches, where relevant to the product use case. Define scientifically justified performance metrics, evaluation methodologies, test cases, and acceptance criteria to assess algorithm performance, including accuracy, robustness, reliability, generalizability, explainability, bias, and subgroup performance. Plan, lead, and execute reproducible scientific evaluations and bench tests using representative datasets and relevant subgroups as part of the overall verification and validation strategy. Interpret scientific and technical evaluation results, conduct detailed error and failure-mode analyses, investigate unexpected findings, and derive evidence-based recommendations for algorithm improvements and product decisions. Assess the clinical and practical relevance of algorithm performance, including the implications of model limitations, data characteristics, and potential failure modes in the intended use environment. Contribute to the design and execution of clinical investigations, reader studies, retrospective or prospective studies, and other evidence-generation activities required to establish algorithm performance and clinical relevance. Collaborate with clinical research and domain experts to ensure that scientific evaluation approaches, study protocols, endpoints, and interpretations are methodologically sound and relevant to real-world use. Take ownership of Data Science work products and scientific documentation, including data management information, data and annotation specifications, algorithm development documentation, scientific evaluation protocols, test cases, and scientific evaluation reports. Provide scientific and technical input into product reviews, design reviews, verification and validation activities, and regulatory submissions. Support responses to questions concerning data, annotations, methodology, clinical relevance, and algorithm performance. Work closely with software engineering and MLOps teams to establish reproducible development pipelines, versioned datasets and models, experiment tracking, automated testing, controlled deployment, and integration of AI/ML components into products. Contribute to the definition and implementation of lifecycle monitoring strategies, including metrics and mechanisms for detecting data anomalies, changes in data distributions, performance degradation, and algorithm drift. Identify technical, scientific, clinical, and data-related risks early and proactively communicate their potential impact on algorithm development, product performance, and regulatory objectives. Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior Data Scientists, support knowledge sharing, and contribute to the development of scientific and technical best practices within the R&D organization. Stay up to date with advances in Data Science, AI/ML, clinical research, biomedical science, and applicable regulatory expectations, assessing their relevance and potential application to ongoing and future product development. Qualification Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Biomedical Engineering, Medical Informatics, Biomedical Sciences, Clinical Research, or another relevant quantitative, scientific, or engineering discipline. A PhD is welcome but not required. Equivalent professional experience in clinical science, biomedical research, medical technology, applied AI/ML research, or a related scientific and technical environment is highly valued. The candidate should have a strong foundation in: Probability, statistics, experimental design, and scientific methodology. Artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning. Linear algebra, optimization, and numerical methods. Data structures, algorithms, and software programming. Clinical research methodology, biomedical research, or applied scientific investigation. Model evaluation, interpretation of empirical results, and evidence-based decision-making. Experience Level This is a Mid-Senior R&D position. The candidate is expected to have approximately 4–8 years of relevant professional experience in Data Science, AI/ML, clinical science, biomedical research, medical technology, or a related applied research and product development environment. The emphasis is on demonstrated ownership and practical experience rather than academic qualifications or years of experience alone. Particularly relevant experience includes: Hands-on development and scientific evaluation of AI/ML models in applied research or product development environments. Experience working with clinical data, biomedical datasets, medical imaging, healthcare applications, or other domain-specific scientific data. Experience designing or contributing to clinical studies, scientific investigations, or structured evidence-generation activities. Experience translating clinical, scientific, or customer requirements into technical specifications and measurable performance criteria. Experience collaborating across multidisciplinary teams, including clinical experts, researchers, engineers, product management, and quality and regulatory stakeholders. Experience taking AI/ML solutions from research and prototyping towards product integration, verification, validation, and deployment. Candidates with a strong background in clinical research, biomedical engineering, medical informatics, or applied healthcare AI are particularly encouraged, even if their professional experience is not exclusively in traditional Data Science roles. Desired Knowledge & Experience Strong understanding of machine learning, deep learning, statistical analysis, experimental design, and scientific evaluation methodologies. Active programming skills in Python and practical experience with libraries and frameworks such as NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Keras. Demonstrated experience in the end-to-end AI/ML development workflow, including data preparation, model development, training, tuning, evaluation, error analysis, reproducibility, and technical documentation. Proven ability to independently define and execute scientific evaluation strategies, including performance metrics, evaluation cohorts, subgroup analyses, test methods, and acceptance criteria. Practical experience in clinical science, biomedical research, medical technology, healthcare AI, or another domain-specific applied research environment. Understanding of clinical research principles, including study design, clinical endpoints, patient populations, data interpretation, and the assessment of clinical relevance. Experience working with clinical or biomedical data, including an understanding of data quality, representativeness, bias, confounding factors, annotation quality, data provenance, and traceability. Demonstrated ability to translate scientific and clinical questions into technical problems and to communicate algorithm performance, limitations, and implications to multidisciplinary stakeholders. Experience contributing to scientific publications, clinical investigations, research reports, technical documentation, or other structured evidence-generation activities. Knowledge of medical device software development, AI/ML product lifecycle management, and relevant quality and regulatory frameworks is an advantage. Familiarity with MLOps concepts and tooling, including source and data versioning, reproducible pipelines, experiment tracking, automated testing, CI/CD, deployment, and performance monitoring. Hands-on experience with current Large Language Models and Generative AI, including foundation models, prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, model adaptation, and fine-tuning. Knowledge of Agentic AI, including tool-using models, multi-step workflows, orchestration, memory, and autonomous or semi-autonomous decision paths, is an advantage. Experience with systematic evaluation of LLM, Generative AI, and Agentic AI systems, including task-specific benchmarks, groundedness, factuality, robustness, reproducibility, human evaluation, safety and guardrail testing, tool-use correctness, and failure-mode analysis. Experience with databases and query languages such as SQL; knowledge of Kusto Query Language, Snowflake, or graph databases such as Neo4j is an advantage. Exposure to cloud-based data and AI environments, preferably Microsoft Azure, including Azure Blob Storage, Azure Databricks, Azure Data Factory, Azure Machine Learning, Azure Monitor, or Azure DevOps. Experience working with structured and unstructured data, including clinical datasets, medical imaging, machine logs, event data, Parquet files, text data, or multimodal data. Knowledge of healthcare, medical technology, clinical data, or interoperability standards such as DICOM, HL7, or FHIR is preferred. Familiarity with medical device development standards and regulatory frameworks, such as ISO 13485, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, and applicable AI-related regulatory requirements, is an advantage. Experience coordinating scientific and technical workstreams, managing project deliverables, and aligning priorities across cross-functional R&D and product development teams. Required Soft Skills & Other Capabilities Strong scientific mindset, analytical thinking, critical reasoning, and attention to detail, with the ability to challenge assumptions and draw objective conclusions from empirical evidence. Ability to independently drive scientific and technical workstreams, take ownership of deliverables, and make well-founded decisions within an agreed scope. Strong interdisciplinary mindset, with the ability to bridge Data Science, clinical science, biomedical research, software engineering, product development, and regulatory considerations. Proven ability to collaborate effectively with clinical experts, researchers, Data Scientists, software developers, product managers, and quality and regulatory stakeholders. Ability to understand and appreciate clinical and scientific context, translating complex domain-specific problems into practical and technically sound AI/ML solutions. Commitment to scientific integrity, reproducibility, traceability, data quality, and responsible AI development. Curiosity and resilience to investigate unexpected results, identify root causes, challenge established approaches, and continuously improve algorithms based on scientific evidence. Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, including the ability to assess technical and scientific risks, identify dependencies, and propose practical solutions. Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including the ability to present and explain complex scientific methods, clinical context, technical results, uncertainties, limitations, and risks to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Ability to take initiative, manage competing priorities, and work independently while recognizing when alignment or guidance from senior technical, clinical, product, or regulatory stakeholders is required. Willingness to share knowledge, mentor junior colleagues, and contribute to a collaborative, scientifically rigorous, and innovation-driven R&D culture.

title: AI Data Engineer (Speech & Language)
description: About the role You will own the data that trains and evaluates every model our AI team builds. Your work feeds pretraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) runs for speech-to-text (STT), large language models (LLM), text-to-speech (TTS), Speech-to-speech (S2S), language identification (LID) and intent prediction etc, all built for Indian languages and code-mixed speech & language. Requirements What you'll do Build training data for every stage of the model lifecycle. Prepare corpora for continued pretraining, instruction and conversation data for SFT, and preference pairs, reward signals and rollout data for RL (DPO, GRPO and similar). Own the data harvesting pipeline end to end. Collect from public web and speech sources, licensed datasets and consented production logs. Clean, deduplicate, filter, redact PII and track provenance and licensing for every sample. Generate synthetic data at scale. Use LLMs to create code-mixed dialogues, intent-labelled utterances and domain conversations; use TTS and audio augmentation (noise, telephony codecs, speed, reverb) to grow speech coverage. Make data model-ready. Output the exact format each training stack expects: chat-templated JSONL, ASR/TTS manifests with aligned transcripts and durations, sharded and packed datasets, with versioning and lineage so every run is reproducible. Build the evaluation pipeline for each model. Curate held-out and production-like test sets per language and domain, and automate metrics: STT: WER/CER per language, code-mixed and entity error rates TTS: intelligibility via ASR round-trip, pronunciation checks, MOS collection LID: accuracy and confusion across languages and scripts Intent: precision, recall, F1 per class LLM: task accuracy, LLM-as-judge rubrics, regression suites Close the loop with production. Learn how the voice agent behaves in real calls, mine failure cases from logs, and turn them into new training and test data. Handle Indic text properly. Unicode normalization (nukta, ZWJ/ZWNJ, matras), numerals and dates, inverse text normalization, transliteration between native script and romanized text, and consistent treatment of code-switched Hindi–English and other language pairs. Ship fast and document. Small, tested, reusable pipeline components; clear dataset cards stating what went in, why, and in what proportion. What we're looking for 1–2 years building data pipelines, ML pipelines or backend systems; strong internships or open-source work count. Strong Python, plus comfort with Linux, Bash, Git and processing large text and audio files efficiently. Working knowledge of how STT, TTS, LLM and classifier models are trained, and what good training data looks like for each (alignment, duration limits, speaker balance, label quality, chat templates). Hands-on use of Hugging Face Datasets, pandas or Polars, and audio tooling such as librosa, torchaudio, sox or ffmpeg. Experience running parallel or distributed jobs (multiprocessing, Ray, Spark or Dask) and working with cloud object storage. Familiarity with Indian languages and scripts: you can spot a broken Unicode sequence, a wrong transliteration or a mislabelled language. Read or speak at least one Indian language besides English. An engineering mindset: you test your pipelines, measure data quality with numbers, and ship a working first version within days, not weeks. Good to have Experience with Indic NLP tooling such as IndicNLP library, IndicTrans2, Aksharamukha or indic-transliteration, and with datasets like IndicVoices, Kathbath or Sangraha. Forced alignment and segmentation (CTC alignment, Montreal Forced Aligner, VAD-based chunking) for long-form audio. Ensemble or model-in-the-loop labelling: combining several ASR or LLM outputs to auto-label data and filter low-confidence samples. Quality filtering techniques: MinHash deduplication, model-based quality classifiers, test-set contamination checks. Exposure to training frameworks the data feeds into: NeMo, ESPnet, Hugging Face TRL, Unsloth or Axolotl. Annotation tooling (Label Studio or similar) and running small human-labelling projects. Benefits You are the person who decides what our models learn from. Data quality is the biggest lever on model quality, and you own it. Work across the full voice stack (STT, LLM, TTS, S2S, LID, intent) instead of one narrow model. Small, early AI team: high ownership from day one Your datasets and evals ship straight into a production voice agent serving Indian-language users.

Your work feeds pretraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) runs for speech-to-text (STT), large language models (LLM), text-to-speech (TTS), Speech-to-speech (S2S), language identification (LID) and intent prediction etc, all built for Indian languages and code-mixed speech & language. Requirements What you'll do Build training data for every stage of the model lifecycle. Prepare corpora for continued pretraining, instruction and conversation data for SFT, and preference pairs, reward signals and rollout data for RL (DPO, GRPO and similar). Own the data harvesting pipeline end to end. Collect from public web and speech sources, licensed datasets and consented production logs. Clean, deduplicate, filter, redact PII and track provenance and licensing for every sample. Generate synthetic data at scale. Use LLMs to create code-mixed dialogues, intent-labelled utterances and domain conversations; use TTS and audio augmentation (noise, telephony codecs, speed, reverb) to grow speech coverage. Make data model-ready. Output the exact format each training stack expects: chat-templated JSONL, ASR/TTS manifests with aligned transcripts and durations, sharded and packed datasets, with versioning and lineage so every run is reproducible. Build the evaluation pipeline for each model. Curate held-out and production-like test sets per language and domain, and automate metrics: STT: WER/CER per language, code-mixed and entity error rates TTS: intelligibility via ASR round-trip, pronunciation checks, MOS collection LID: accuracy and confusion across languages and scripts Intent: precision, recall, F1 per class LLM: task accuracy, LLM-as-judge rubrics, regression suites Close the loop with production. Learn how the voice agent behaves in real calls, mine failure cases from logs, and turn them into new training and test data. Handle Indic text properly. Unicode normalization (nukta, ZWJ/ZWNJ, matras), numerals and dates, inverse text normalization, transliteration between native script and romanized text, and consistent treatment of code-switched Hindi–English and other language pairs. Ship fast and document. Small, tested, reusable pipeline components; clear dataset cards stating what went in, why, and in what proportion. What we're looking for 1–2 years building data pipelines, ML pipelines or backend systems; strong internships or open-source work count. Strong Python, plus comfort with Linux, Bash, Git and processing large text and audio files efficiently. Working knowledge of how STT, TTS, LLM and classifier models are trained, and what good training data looks like for each (alignment, duration limits, speaker balance, label quality, chat templates). Hands-on use of Hugging Face Datasets, pandas or Polars, and audio tooling such as librosa, torchaudio, sox or ffmpeg. Experience running parallel or distributed jobs (multiprocessing, Ray, Spark or Dask) and working with cloud object storage. Familiarity with Indian languages and scripts: you can spot a broken Unicode sequence, a wrong transliteration or a mislabelled language. Read or speak at least one Indian language besides English. An engineering mindset: you test your pipelines, measure data quality with numbers, and ship a working first version within days, not weeks. Good to have Experience with Indic NLP tooling such as IndicNLP library, IndicTrans2, Aksharamukha or indic-transliteration, and with datasets like IndicVoices, Kathbath or Sangraha. Forced alignment and segmentation (CTC alignment, Montreal Forced Aligner, VAD-based chunking) for long-form audio. Ensemble or model-in-the-loop labelling: combining several ASR or LLM outputs to auto-label data and filter low-confidence samples. Quality filtering techniques: MinHash deduplication, model-based quality classifiers, test-set contamination checks. Exposure to training frameworks the data feeds into: NeMo, ESPnet, Hugging Face TRL, Unsloth or Axolotl. Annotation tooling (Label Studio or similar) and running small human-labelling projects. Benefits You are the person who decides what our models learn from. Data quality is the biggest lever on model quality, and you own it. Work across the full voice stack (STT, LLM, TTS, S2S, LID, intent) instead of one narrow model. Small, early AI team: high ownership from day one Your datasets and evals ship straight into a production voice agent serving Indian-language users.

Experience & Qualifications ● Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field. ● 10+ years of experience in DevOps, cloud infrastructure, information security, or DevSecOps. ● Strong hands-on experience securing AWS environments and managing enterprise CI/CD pipelines. ● Experience with Infrastructure as Code, Kubernetes, container security, and automation. ● Good understanding of networking and cloud connectivity troubleshooting. ● Experience supporting production environments, handling critical incidents, and leading technical initiatives. About the Business LexisNexis Risk Solutions is the essential partner in the assessment of risk. Within our Business Services vertical, we offer a multitude of solutions focused on helping businesses of all sizes drive higher revenue growth, maximize operational efficiencies, and improve customer experience. Our solutions help our customers solve difficult problems in the areas of Anti-Money Laundering/Counter Terrorist Financing, Identity Authentication & Verification, Fraud and Credit Risk mitigation and Customer Data Management. We own the infrastructure, deployment pipelines, observability and security posture for a portfolio of Java-based services and data pipelines. We are currently modernizing our platform by moving workloads from Kubernetes (AKS) to Azure Container Apps, so it's a great time to join and help shape how our services are built and run. The role combines infrastructure-as-code, platform engineering, release engineering and operational support. You will work closely with development, QA, security, release management and central platform teams to deliver automation, observability, compliance and platform modernization initiatives. Design, build and operate Azure infrastructure using Terraform, and maintain Kubernetes (AKS) clusters and Helm-based deployments to build and improve CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions, including image promotion, GitOps (ArgoCD) and blue/green releases. Drive container and supply chain security: hardened/FIPS-compliant images, vulnerability scanning and remediation, and FedRAMP compliance controls, in partnership with InfoSec and improve observability through monitoring, logging, tracing, synthetic checks, dashboards, alerting and SLOs. Manage secrets, identities and TLS certificates, including automated rotation and renewal, cloud networking, including VNet peering, private endpoints, DNS and firewall rules as code. Track and report on vulnerabilities and compliance, and keep container registries, artifacts and Terraform state well maintained. Participate in release coordination, change management, disaster recovery, blue/green failover and capacity planning and identify recurring issues and automate operational toil to improve reliability and developer productivity. Partner with development, QA, database, security and operations teams to promote operational excellence and continuous improvement. Strong knowledge of containers, Kubernetes, Helm, cloud networking, IAM/RBAC and distributed systems. Proficiency with Terraform and Infrastructure-as-Code practices across multiple environments. Experience with GitHub Actions or equivalent CI/CD tooling, including GitOps and progressive delivery (ArgoCD, Argo Rollouts). Experience securing container workloads, including image hardening, vulnerability remediation (e.g., Wiz, Defender, Xray), secrets management (HashiCorp Vault, Akeyless) and compliance controls; FedRAMP experience is a plus. Experience with observability tools such as Elastic, Grafana, Prometheus and Open Telemetry. Strong incident management skills, including technical recovery, RCA facilitation and corrective actions. Experience with Linux administration and scripting in Bash, Python or PowerShell. title: Principal Site Reliability Engineer
description: Ready to be a Titan? We're looking for a Principal Site Reliability Engineer to join our Site Reliability & Infrastructure Engineering team. We run entirely on the cloud, and this team owns production intelligence, reliability, and operational automation — moving from reactive incident response toward systems that observe, correlate, reason, and act. We're building the next generation of SRE: not dashboards and runbooks, but agents and automation that make our platform self-aware and self-healing at scale. At Principal level, you won't just operate the platform — you'll define how we think about reliability across the entire engineering organization. You'll set the technical direction, establish the standards, and be the person other engineers turn to when the hardest infrastructure problems need to be solved. We make a huge impact on thousands of companies in the U.S. and abroad by enabling them to be more efficient and effective at running their business. We have a cultural foundation built on diversity, inclusion, and innovation, and we want you and your ideas to thrive at ServiceTitan. Come join us. Lead the design and delivery of major platform initiatives: Kubernetes infrastructure, observability frameworks, SLO programs, and incident management systems. Partner with Engineering Managers, Staff Engineers, and product engineering leadership to review architecture and infrastructure decisions before they ship — and hold the bar on non-functional requirements across the org. Identify systemic reliability risks before they become incidents, and drive remediation across teams with org-wide impact. Define and operationalize SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets across ServiceTitan's platform — not just within the SRE team, but as a standard every engineering team adopts. Drive adoption of reliability and observability best practices across engineering — through documentation, design reviews, and direct partnership with product teams. Design and build AI-assisted operational systems — agents that correlate production telemetry, diagnose failure patterns, recommend or execute remediation, and participate safely in deployment decisions. Move routine investigation and triage from humans to automation, while preserving human judgment for high-risk changes. Partner with Infrastructure Engineering on deployment safety — progressive delivery, canary analysis, and AI-assisted promotion decisions that answer "is there enough production evidence to continue this deployment?" not just "did the deployment complete?" Mentor Staff and Senior SREs, raising the technical ceiling of the team through code reviews, architecture feedback, and direct pairing on complex problems. Contribute to the technical hiring bar — participate in system design interviews and help define what Principal-level looks like at ServiceTitan. What You'll Bring Kubernetes (must-have): deep, expert-level understanding of Kubernetes as a system — not just operations, but internals, failure modes, capacity planning, and large-scale cluster management. SRE principles: proven experience defining and operationalizing SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets across an engineering organization — able to speak to how you drove adoption, not just how you implemented them on your own team. Observability at scale: deep expertise with a modern observability stack (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, or Elasticsearch) and the ability to design observability frameworks that work org-wide, not just per-service. Cloud engineering & networking: expert grounding in AWS, GCP, or Azure — including networking fundamentals, security, and cost optimization at scale. Distributed systems depth: able to reason through complex failure modes (retry storms, cascading failures, thundering herds, timeout propagation) and architect systems that degrade gracefully under pressure. Incident management: track record of leading major incident response, driving blameless postmortems, and implementing systemic fixes — not just resolving individual incidents. CI/CD and delivery safety: deep experience with CI/CD systems, progressive delivery, and the ability to improve pipeline reliability and safety at org scale. AI in operations: experience building or deploying AI-assisted operational capabilities in production — automated investigation, anomaly correlation, remediation agents, or deployment safety systems. We're not looking for hackathon prototypes; we want engineers who have shipped AI tooling that production systems depend on. 12+ years of relevant hands-on experience, with a clear track record of technical leadership on complex, cross-team infrastructure initiatives at product companies operating at scale. About You You've operated at Staff or Principal level before and know what it means to own a technical domain — not just execute within it. You're the person Engineering Managers and VPs call when a system needs to be rethought, not just fixed. You can set direction with incomplete information, make architectural trade-offs explicit, and build consensus across teams without needing organizational authority to do it. You care about reliability the way a product engineer cares about user experience — it's not overhead, it's the product. You measure your success not by what you personally shipped, but by how much better the entire engineering organization runs because of the standards and systems you put in place. You're drawn to the question of what operations looks like when AI agents handle the repetitive analysis and humans own the judgment calls — and you want to be the engineer who designs that boundary. ‌ Be Human With Us: Being human isn’t about checking every box on a list. It’s about the experiences we have, people we meet, and the perspectives we share. So, if you have the skills but are hesitant to apply because of your background, apply anyway. Product adoption and agreed business, user, data, and service measures improve over time; RunOps feedback informs roadmap and backlog decisions. Experience leading delivery with engineering and architecture teams and coordinating dependencies across multiple teams or functions. Experience supporting live digital products, including service performance, incidents/problems, releases, operational readiness, and continuous improvement. Experience communicating technical options, decisions, risks, and priorities to business and technology stakeholders. Experience in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, or another regulated or quality-focused environment. Experience with enterprise architecture, data governance, data quality, metadata, privacy, cybersecurity, and cloud/platform operating models. Experience with Agile product delivery and tools such as Jira, Confluence, or equivalent backlog and collaboration platforms; familiarity with IT service management practices. Experience supporting product financials, investment planning, vendor or resource management, and adoption/change activities. Functional and Leadership Skills Product strategy, roadmap development, backlog ordering, outcome measurement, and lifecycle management. Strong technical judgment and ability to understand data, analytics, integration, architecture, and operational trade-offs without needing to perform hands-on engineering. Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to tailor complex technical information to business audiences and global teams. Structured problem solving, sound judgment, accountability, prioritization, and the ability to resolve ambiguity and escalate at the right time. Collaborative leadership, customer and user focus, adaptability, and effectiveness across distributed teams and time zones.

The role defines and monitors SLOs, instruments platforms for observability, leads incident response through to permanent prevention, and applies AI and automation for anomaly detection, predictive alerting and self-healing. It also coaches platform engineering teams in reliability practice and error-budget discipline. The role sits in Reliability Engineering & Operations and is deployed into a platform domain while drawing on the central capability, so it holds the central reliability standard inside a team it does not report to. Platform build and engineering direction sit with the Principal Engineers and the Engineering Director, the major incident process sits with the Major Incident Manager, and the reliability standard itself is set by the Reliability Engineering Senior Director. Reliability targets are held jointly with the Platform Manager rather than imposed on them. ROLE SCALE AND COMPLEXITY This is a senior enterprise reliability leadership role operating across globally distributed, business-critical cloud and hosting services. The post holder is accountable for setting technical direction, resolving systemic and ambiguous reliability risks, and influencing prioritisation across multiple platform teams, suppliers and geographies without relying on direct line authority. The role manages a portfolio of interdependent services with material operational, regulatory, cyber, resilience and financial consequences. It shapes investment and supplier decisions and may influence or govern an annual technology and service portfolio of up to approximately GBP 23 million, where applicable to the assigned scope. MARKET SCOPE Global scope, supporting business operations across regions, countries and markets in which GSK operates. The role establishes consistent reliability outcomes across regional delivery teams while accommodating local regulatory, data-residency, business-continuity and market-criticality requirements. Key Responsibilities Define and monitor SLOs for the platforms served, and instrument those platforms for observability so reliability is measured rather than assumed. Apply AI and automation for anomaly detection, predictive alerting and self-healing, so that recurring conditions are handled without human intervention. Lead incident response for the platforms served, and drive root-cause resolution through to permanent prevention rather than closing on restoration. Improve resilience through capacity, failover and recovery engineering, and test recovery rather than documenting it. Reduce operational toil through automation and reusable tooling, working the identified manual task and toil candidates and evidencing the effort removed. Close observability coverage gaps for the platforms served, prioritising by the reliability risk each gap leaves unmeasured. Coach platform engineering teams in reliability practice and error-budget discipline, so reliability is built in rather than inspected in. Track reliability metrics against SLOs and team OKRs, and act on the trend rather than only reporting it. Support reliability oversight of supplier-run services, holding partner-operated components to the same SLOs as internal ones. Hold the central reliability standard while deployed in a platform domain, escalating to the Reliability Engineering Senior Director where local pressure would erode it. Feed reliability evidence into the platform backlog held by the Product Owner, so that resilience work competes on stated risk rather than on goodwill. Hold the boundaries with the Principal Engineers on platform build, the Major Incident Manager on the major incident process, and the Platform Manager on the reliability targets the platform commits to. Set the multi-year reliability strategy and engineering roadmap for the assigned cloud and hosting portfolio, translating enterprise risk and business priorities into funded reliability outcomes. Own cross-platform reliability governance, including service tiering, SLO policy, error-budget decisions, resilience exceptions and common engineering standards across internal and supplier-operated services. Lead resolution of complex, high-impact and systemic failure modes spanning cloud, hosting, network, security, applications and third-party dependencies, with authority to convene senior technical and service leaders. Provide evidence-based recommendations for investment, risk acceptance and supplier performance decisions, including prioritisation across a material service portfolio and, where delegated, spend of up to approximately GBP 25 million. AIOps and operations automation, covering anomaly detection, predictive alerting and self-healing. Why is this level of Education Required? An engineering grounding is needed because the role writes the automation and instrumentation itself and must be credible to platform engineers whose systems it is changing. Job-Related Experience Overall 15 Years and typically 10-12+ years in infrastructure, cloud, platform or reliability engineering, including significant experience leading enterprise-scale reliability outcomes across multiple teams or service domains. 5+ years of hands-on SRE, Reliability Engineering, or Cloud Operations experience. Experience supporting large-scale production cloud and hosting environments. Experience owning operational reliability for critical business services. Proven record of improving service availability, resiliency, and operational efficiency. Demonstrated accountability for globally distributed, 24x7, business-critical services and for decisions with material operational, regulatory, customer or financial impact. Proven ability to influence Directors, Senior Directors and VP-level stakeholders, including presenting options, quantified risk, trade-offs and investment recommendations. Experience governing strategic suppliers and complex service ecosystems, with exposure to substantial technology budgets or portfolios; direct budget ownership is desirable but not mandatory where strong investment influence is evidenced. Track record of setting technical direction, leading through ambiguity and developing senior engineering capability across organisational and geographic boundaries. Reliability & Operations Experience defining and operating: SLIs , SLOs, Error Budgets, Operational KPIs Experience leading: Major incident response, post-incident reviews, Root-cause analysis , Capacity management, Resiliency and recovery testing.
